goal: An AI assistant that can do chart analysis, Pine Script development, workflow automation, bandarmology, drawing, alerts and UI automation on IDX stocks — showing the exact same data Stockbit shows.

features.name: Chart analysis
features.detail: Indicator readings, pivot-clustered support/resistance, SVG candles with overlays and sub-panels, 16 candlestick patterns, and daily/weekly/monthly alignment.
features.verified: Live: 220 sessions for BBRI in 19 requests; indicators computed and cross-checked.

features.name: Bandarmology
features.detail: Broker summary plus a broker-to-broker distribution Sankey showing who accumulated from whom. Date ranges and market boards supported.
features.verified: Cross-checked against Stockbit screenshots for BRMS, TPIA and PSAB.

features.name: Pine Script development
features.detail: TradingView Pine v6: indicators, strategies, alert conditions, and Stockbit-derived levels embedded as constants. One script per pane.
features.verified: Generated and structurally validated; runs with no API call when levels are excluded.

features.name: Drawing
features.detail: Levels, zones, trend lines, channels and markers drawn on the REAL Stockbit chart, by driving the browser you logged in with over CDP in a visible window; Stockbit's own auto-save persists them. The same geometry is also rendered as SVG and embedded in generated Pine. Saved layouts and their drawings are readable and writable over REST.
features.verified: The endpoints the chart page's own save adapter uses were read out of the current web bundle: /chartbit/charts and /chartbit/chart-drawings, content base64-ZIP of a single layout.json. The per-symbol pair this project targeted for months is a server-side stub and has been removed. Codec round-trip, shape mapping and the page scripts are tested; two tests drive a real Chromium when one is installed.

features.name: Alerts
features.detail: Rule engine sharing one indicator registry with the Pine emitter, so an alert and its alertcondition agree — plus a standalone daemon (`stockbit-alerts watch`) that polls during IDX hours and delivers. Three channels: an append-only JSONL log (always, written first), a native desktop notification (default on, no setup), and an optional https webhook. Fires once per bar; reports warm-up separately from a false condition.
features.verified: Live: two rules fired on BBRI with correct values (close 3020 > 2000; RSI 56.18 < 70), Windows toasts delivered, log written; the next pass fired 0, confirming same-bar suppression.

features.name: Workflow automation
features.detail: Five saved recipes — deep_dive, morning_scan, bandar_watch, alert_sweep, pine_handoff — each running several tools in one call, the same way every time. Declarative steps only: no eval, a closed template vocabulary, capped fan-out that reports what it skipped, and a failing step that aborts and names itself unless marked optional.
features.verified: Live: deep_dive on BBRI ran all four steps green in 3.7s (quote, technicals, chart, broker distribution).

features.name: UI automation on graphics
features.detail: Reframed rather than declined. Driving Stockbit Desktop is still refused — it is Tauri/WKWebView with no CDP, and it is a thin client over the same JSON API this server already reads. What the request actually meant is drawing on the real chart, and that is done by driving the BROWSER you logged in with. ADR-0005.

features.name: Backtesting
features.detail: Nine preset strategies plus custom conditions in the same grammar the alerts and the Pine emitter share. Next-bar fills, stops win ties, gaps fill at the open, ARA/ARB-locked sessions are unfillable, buy-and-hold benchmarked over the same window. Walk-forward with a verdict that reaches 'inconclusive' before it reaches 'robust'.
features.verified: Absence of lookahead proved structurally: a backtest over the first N bars is a prefix of the backtest over all bars, asserted across nine presets, three cut points and 100+ trades.

features.name: Universe screening
features.detail: One condition across many symbols, with pre-dispatch budgets and honest truncation. Universe sources: explicit symbols, movers, trending, your own watchlists and your saved screens. Ad-hoc screens run without creating anything; saving one is a separate, confirm-gated tool.

features.name: The full read surface
features.detail: One module per section of the Stockbit web UI: stream and research, company profile and fundamentals, insider activity, market internals and running trade, the broker directory and league table, corporate actions and the dividend calendar, and the screener catalogue.
features.verified: Every route is declared in the closed table and snapshotted per host by test/transport.test.ts. Routes nobody has observed live say so in their tool descriptions and project defensively rather than renaming fields on a guess.

features.name: Portfolio and order entry
features.detail: Portfolio, positions, cash and buying power, open orders, trade and realised history, performance, fee schedule, tradability and a masked account identity — plus order entry: preview a ticket, show it to the user, then buy, sell, amend or cancel against that ticket id. OFF by default and unreachable from a saved workflow recipe.
features.verified: Not against a live account, and deliberately so: reading this host needs the trading PIN, which this project never stores. The apparatus is tested against a fake brokerage that lies in every way a real one can — accepts and hides the order, errors after accepting it, errors without accepting it, fails the read-back. Every refusal path asserts that ZERO requests left the process.
features.blocker: The first REAL order is a live gate, not a test run: a HAR of one manually-placed order settles platform_order_type, the error envelope and the list shape, then one 1-lot order with the account owner watching. docs/PENDING-VERIFICATION.md carries the protocol.

features.name: e-IPO
features.detail: The offerings, one offering in full, where it is in its timetable, this account's own subscription and what was ALLOTTED, the RDN cash it is funded from, and subscribing under the same switch and the same two-step protocol as an exchange order.
features.verified: Not against a live account. The session is minted from the ordinary login through a webview grant, and the preview uses Stockbit's OWN verify endpoint — the server knows the offering's rules and this project does not.
features.blocker: Same live gate as order entry, on an open offering.

features.name: Account writes
features.detail: Watchlist create, rename, delete, add, remove and favourite; screener save, delete and favourite. Each confirm-gated, verified by reading the account back, and logged. Deleting a watchlist that still holds symbols refuses once and names the count.
features.verified: Every edit reads the account back, so a wrong body shape reports not-visible rather than a false success. Nothing rolls back: each of these is one action a person can reverse in the Stockbit app, and undoing a change we could not read would be a second blind write.

verification.check: Volume unit is LOTS, not shares
verification.evidence: BBRI value/volume = 303,668 against an average price of 3,037 — exactly price x 100.
BBRI, TLKM, GOTO: zero levels labelled support above the close or resistance below it. Was broken; fixed in 1c4e52c.
220 sessions (2025-09-03 to 2026-08-05) in 19 requests, not truncated.

verification.check: The write boundary is enumerated, not assumed
verification.evidence: Every non-GET route is sorted into a named class citing the ADR that admitted it: session refresh, Chartbit persistence (ADR-0003), the four order routes plus the e-IPO pair (ADR-0004), and watchlist/screener edits (ADR-0006), with a fifth class for POSTs that read. test/transport.test.ts asserts nothing else mutates, and test/tools.test.ts asserts on a real server that exactly twelve tools can change anything and that none of them is reachable from a saved workflow recipe.
BBRI 2026-08-05, REGULER board, IDR: 8 brokers charted, returned in 156ms as part of the deep_dive workflow.

verification.check: Workflows run end to end on live data
verification.evidence: deep_dive on BBRI: quote 388ms, technicals 2542ms, chart 630ms, brokers 156ms — no step failed.

verification.check: Alert daemon fires and delivers on live data
verification.evidence: BBRI: 'close > 2000' fired at 3020 and 'rsi14 < 70' at 56.18; Windows toasts delivered, both logged; a second pass fired 0.

blockers: Chartbit writes are ENABLED under ADR-0003 with their full apparatus (snapshot, verify, rollback, mutation log) — and Stockbit's end discards them. Both POST routes answer 200 and store nothing; eliminated across nine variables, and their own web bundle has no save wiring either. Not a blocker this project can clear.

Composing brand-new drawings needs the TradingView line-tool schema (what `state` a LineToolHorzLine expects). Stockbit serves the charting library only to an authenticated chart page, so it could not be read the way the rest of the format was. Reading, round-tripping and modifying an existing layout does not need it.
notes: The Chartbit daily-price route was added and then removed: it answers HTTP 200 but returns an empty payload for every parameterization tried. The runtime cross-check rejected it and fell back, so no wrong bar was ever produced.
Two sub-agents are installed for this project: stockbit-verifier (does each feature do what was asked) and stockbit-bug-hunter (what is wrong that nobody asked about).

2026-08-09: eight shipped defects fixed (morning_scan aborted on every run; top_movers sent a spelling Stockbit does not use; broker_summary sent three non-existent enums; getBars with `to` and no `from` returned a remnant of the requested window while reporting truncated:false). Then backtesting, walk-forward, candlestick patterns, multi-timeframe and universe scan. 496 tests, up from 362.
